title: Bangladesh Stun Australia With Historic Nine-Wicket Test Victory in Darwin
excerpt: In one of Test cricket's greatest upsets, Bangladesh thrashed the world's top-ranked side on their own soil, powered by Hasan Mahmud's nine wickets and Tanzid Hasan's century.
body:
• Bangladesh defeated Australia by nine wickets in Darwin on Sunday — their first-ever Test win on Australian soil and only their second victory over Australia in any format.
  • Hasan Mahmud earned Player of the Match with nine wickets, including a devastating 6-55 that bowled Australia out for just 198 in the first innings.
  • Mehidy Hasan Miraz was the all-round hero: 65 runs with the bat, a catch-and-bowl of Steve Smith, and five wickets in Australia's second innings.
  • The result could significantly impact the World Test Championship standings, with India and other Asian sides watching closely.

The Upset That Rewrites Cricket History

Bangladesh chased down 57 runs to complete a landmark nine-wicket victory over Australia in the series opener at Marrara Oval in Darwin on Sunday, delivering one of Test cricket's greatest upsets. Mominul Haque cut Beau Webster to the fence for the winning runs, triggering jubilant celebrations from the touring squad and their vocal fans in the stands.

https://x.com/SriLankaTweet/status/2088885635079897450

Flooring a full-strength Australia — the world's top-ranked Test nation — in their own backyard will be regarded as the South Asian nation's finest victory in 26 years of playing the longest format. It was only Bangladesh's second Test win over Australia, after their maiden victory in Dhaka in 2017.

"This is the biggest win so far for Bangladesh in any format. We will do something special in the future."

— Najmul Hossain Shanto, Bangladesh captain

Hasan Mahmud's Match-Defining Spell

The 26-year-old fast bowler was the destroyer-in-chief. On day one, after Pat Cummins won the toss and elected to bat on a grassy pitch, Hasan ripped through Australia's lineup with figures of 6-55 — the third-best bowling figures by a Bangladesh fast bowler in Test history. He removed both openers, with Jake Weatherald edging a loose drive to the slips and Travis Head chopping onto his stumps.

Australia managed just 198 in the first innings, their lowest total in seven Tests against Bangladesh. Steve Smith's 71 was the only meaningful contribution; no other batter passed 30.

Hasan returned in the second innings to claim three more wickets, finishing with match figures of 9 wickets — including the crucial scalp of Cameron Green, who had scored a defiant century before playing onto his stumps for 104.

Miraz: The Complete All-Round Performance

If Hasan was the pace spearhead, Mehidy Hasan Miraz was the match's most versatile performer. He scored a crucial 65 at number seven in Bangladesh's first innings of 426, marshalling the tail expertly. Then he caught-and-bowled Steve Smith for 44 on day three. On the final day, he took four more wickets — dismissing Alex Carey (caught behind for 30), Beau Webster (bowled for 5), Pat Cummins (caught at bat-pad for 8), and Nathan Lyon (lbw for 15) to wrap up Australia's innings at 284.

"It was excellent, a great moment for us. The way we are playing shows our character. Everything was perfect."

— Mehidy Hasan Miraz

Tanzid Hasan's majestic 101 in the first innings had given Bangladesh the platform, helping them build a commanding 228-run lead that Australia could never overcome despite Green's lone-hand century.

A Pace Revolution Bears Fruit

Captain Shanto attributed the breakthrough to a mindset shift among Bangladesh's young fast bowlers. Remarkably, all 10 Australian wickets in the first innings fell to pace — a statement performance for a nation traditionally associated with spin.

"Earlier, five years ago, pacers didn't want to play Tests," Shanto said. "But we've been playing lots of Test cricket and they are giving importance to the Test format. They want to play, want to perform, want to be world-class."

Bangladesh achieved this result despite missing leading quicks Nahid Rana and Shoriful Islam to injury, making the win even more impressive.

What It Means for India and the WTC

The result sends shockwaves through the World Test Championship standings. Australia, as the reigning WTC leaders, can ill afford such a result at home. For India, watching from afar, Australia's vulnerability is both an opportunity and a warning — South Asian pace attacks are maturing rapidly, and Bangladesh's willingness to embrace conditions outside the subcontinent is reshaping the competitive landscape.

Bangladesh head to the second and final Test in Mackay, Queensland, starting August 22, with a realistic shot at their first-ever Test series win over Australia. For a cricketing nation that has spent decades being dismissed as also-rans, Darwin represents a seismic moment.
nri_angle: The result reshapes the World Test Championship race and demonstrates the growing competitiveness of South Asian cricket, with implications for India's own path to the WTC final.
